title: pkix-dane-resolver: report a signed negative answer as authenticated denial
description:
## What

A DNSSEC-signed NODATA or NXDOMAIN is an authenticated denial: the domain has signed a statement that it publishes no TLSA record. pkix-dane models this -- TlsaResponse::is_authenticated_denial is true for a Secure response with no records -- and documents it as a stronger statement than an unsigned answer, because the client knows nothing was stripped.

pkix-dane-resolver 0.2.0 does not produce it. classify_lookup_error maps hickory's no-records-found to DnssecStatus::Indeterminate with an empty record set, so is_authenticated_denial is never true in practice.

## Why it was left that way

Indeterminate is the fail-closed reading and behaves correctly under the opportunistic policy from PKIX-j32w.4: it does not authenticate, and it permits PKIX fallback, which is right for 'this domain appears to publish no TLSA record'. Reporting Secure for a negative answer that had NOT been validated would be the one direction that is unsafe, so the conservative mapping went in rather than a guess.

## Why it still matters

The distinction is real. A signed denial means DANE is deliberately absent and the client can rely on that; an unsigned or unvalidatable nothing means the client learned nothing and an attacker may have removed the records. A consumer implementing a strict DANE policy, or one that wants to log why DANE did not apply, cannot currently tell those apart.

## Fix

Get the negative answer's DNSSEC proof. hickory's NetError carries the SOA for a no-records case (error.rs has a soa accessor on the NoRecordsFound variant), and records carry a proof field. Determine whether the proof on the SOA or the authority section is reachable through the public API; if it is not, that is an upstream gap worth raising with hickory rather than working around.

## Acceptance

[ ] A signed NODATA for a name in a signed zone yields Secure with no records, so is_authenticated_denial is true
[ ] An unsigned or unvalidatable negative answer still yields Insecure or Indeterminate, never Secure
[ ] Tested against a signed zone with no TLSA at the queried name -- good.dane.huque.com's zone can supply one, and the test needs a DNSSEC-transparent upstream per PKIX_DANE_RESOLVER_TEST_UPSTREAM
